subtype: Approach: copying a topper's timetable without fit [Pitfall]
passage: Sunday night. It is over. Two weeks ago I copied Damini's timetable from her post: wake at 5, study till midnight, one hour of break in total. She looked so calm in the photo! Week one I was fine, proud even. But school starts at 7:30 and I am useless after ten. By Thursday I was nodding through Chemistry, on Friday I slept through the alarm, and today I lay on the bed and could not open a single book. I was so tired I threw out the whole timetable, even the good parts. Now I have nothing, and nine weeks to boards. Damini's routine works for Damini. Somehow I forgot to ask what works for me. Rajni

qa.q: At what time did the copied timetable have Rajni wake up?
qa.a: The copied timetable had Rajni wake up at 5.

qa.q: What is Rajni feeling as the entry ends?
qa.a: Exhausted, discouraged and a bit regretful about throwing out even the useful parts. 😔
Build a schedule around Rajni's own energy and school hours, giving the hard subjects the hours when concentration is best.

qa.q: How might Damini see Rajni's failed routine?
qa.a: As a sign that a routine made for one person may not suit another, since Damini's plan works for Damini.

grounding: Rajni adopts a 5 am to midnight routine from a social media post without fitting it to Rajni's own energy and school hours, and abandons the whole schedule.

subtype: Approach: copying a topper's timetable without fit [Pitfall]
passage: In Amandeep's village the school bus left at half past six and got back at four, and most evenings she helped her mother with the buffaloes before dinner. Then Wasim, the class topper, posted his board-exam routine on a video site: up at five, study till midnight, every day. Half the class shared it. Amandeep copied it into her notebook in neat blue ink. For the first week she dragged herself up at five and sat by the lantern through the power cuts, eyes stinging. By the ninth day she was nodding off on the bus and snapping at her little brother. On the eleventh night her mother found her asleep with her cheek on the Physics book. The next morning Amandeep tore the page out of her notebook. She didn't make a new timetable. She didn't study at all that week.

qa.q: When did the school bus leave and get back?
qa.a: It left at half past six and got back at four.

qa.q: What does Amandeep's behaviour by the ninth day suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She was nodding off on the bus and snapping at her little brother, which shows she was exhausted and irritable.

qa.q: What would you change first in Amandeep's plan?
qa.a: Fit it to her own day, with the long bus hours, the evening chores and the times she feels fresh, instead of copying Wasim's hours.

qa.q: What might Amandeep's mother feel, finding her asleep on the Physics book?
qa.a: She may feel worried and sad, seeing how hard her daughter has been pushing and how tired she has become.

grounding: Shows a student copying a topper's 5am-to-midnight routine that ignores her own day, becoming exhausted and abandoning study planning.
